sentences.text: Sophie Grant attended the meeting as a housing solicitor.
Lee Whitfield (client) attended the meeting.
The purpose of the meeting was to discuss the flat tenancy and rent arrears.
Lee Whitfield lost his job in January at a depot.
The Universal Credit housing element took a long time to process, and the rent arrears accumulated due to this delay.
The arrears amount to £3,850, for three to four months.
Court papers were received by Lee Whitfield.
The hearing date is 9 December at Harbridge County Court.
The possession claim is on rent arrears grounds, specifically grounds 8, 10, and 11, by Ashcroft Lettings.
The landlord is a private landlord.
Lee Whitfield has lived in the flat for six years.
Lee Whitfield lives alone with a cat.
The landlord did not offer a payment plan; Lee offered £50 per month in September, which was rejected.
The offer of £50 per month was made in September and was made via text message.
The damp issue is in the bedroom, with black mould on the wall.
Lee has photos of the damp issue.
Council tax arrears have triggered a bailiff letter.
Lee has a credit card debt of approximately £2,000.
Electricity is now on a meter.
Lee has no support from family or friends for debt issues.
Lee stopped opening accounts or managing finances after losing his job.
Lee took an overdose of 16 paracetamol in March after receiving the first rent arrears letter.
A neighbour found Lee and called an ambulance; he was admitted overnight.
After hospital admission, a nurse contacted Lee a couple of times, then no further follow-up.
Lee has not hurt himself since March.
Lee thought about ending his life on Sunday night, this week, before the court date.
Lee is currently safe and stable today.
Lee said that talking about the situation helps him feel a bit better.
The solicitor advised that the client has a defence based on the housing element failure and the damp issue as a potential counterclaim.
The solicitor will file a defence and a counterclaim for the damp issue.
